mechanism.summary: Represent ordinary ObjectRef ownership with one inline strong-count word while no weak observer exists, and lazily allocate a separate weak-control record only when a cache or enumeration site requests ObjectWeakRef.
mechanism.generality: The representation applies to every ordinary ObjectRef based only on whether that object has a weak observer. It never examines source text, function identity, property names, benchmark paths, inputs, iteration counts, or results. All object operations retain their existing ownership API; object caches and enumeration caches retain non-owning weak semantics, while objects without weak observers avoid Rc's permanently allocated weak-count word.
semantic_risks: preserving strong clone and final-drop behavior, including overflow handling and exactly-once ObjectData destruction
preserving ObjectWeakRef identity, upgrade, clone, and final weak-drop behavior after the last strong reference disappears
ensuring bytecode property and enumeration caches remain non-owning and cannot resurrect or retain an unreachable object
preserving stable object address identity while strong or weak handles exist, including prototype and cyclic-reference behavior
keeping every unsafe pointer conversion localized, aligned, and valid only for the allocation lifetime described by the reference state machine

profile_evidence.source: macOS current-main profile /tmp/qjs-current-external.Vyd00J/hash-map.sample (SHA below) plus MallocStackLogging receipt /tmp/qjs-current-external.Vyd00J/hash-map.malloc-count (SHA-256 eee73db39feb1ca373f275f4b6f6e43b93af457b770854e940fc37c4def5bdc1). The rebuilt current-main release SHA-256 is 568549b735c590a0787d93a84f67d2f3c65312f917e863714a1bb28e6f757ad4 and is runtime-identical to queue candidate 32a00b0e outside evidence-only commits. The live allocation trace recorded 23,760 ObjectRef::with_prototype_slot allocations totaling 3,801,600 bytes and 23,759 PropertyStorage::insert allocations totaling 5,322,016 bytes under the repeated Entry constructor route.
profile_evidence.shared_cost: The rank-two 5.351608x QuickJS-NG gap repeatedly allocates ordinary ObjectData through Rc even though production ObjectWeakRef use is restricted to two bounded bytecode cache families. A lazy weak sidecar can lower the common object allocation class without changing the property-storage mechanisms that were already rejected.

profile_evidence.source: macOS current-main profile /tmp/qjs-current-external.Vyd00J/ai-astar.sample (SHA below) plus MallocStackLogging receipt /tmp/qjs-current-external.Vyd00J/ai-astar-runtime.malloc-count (SHA-256 5f31094a79f13360cb30d5490ceff0181712b5ad2a30bee26cfade76287e8d3a). The independent A* run recorded 10,000 ObjectRef::with_prototype_slot allocations totaling 1,600,000 bytes before its heavier per-node property-storage allocations.
profile_evidence.shared_cost: A* independently creates the same Rc-backed ordinary object headers, confirming that the reference-header mechanism is broader than Entry construction. Its larger property vectors make it a conservative regression sentinel rather than a promised co-target.
